\chapter{Worth the Effort}

\begin{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সার্থক} (sārthôk)}{সার্থক (sārthôk)}]{\bn{সার্থক} (sārthôk) — worthwhile; fruitful}

\label{lesson:BN-C383-sarthok}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to keep up, then the Bengali for to amend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সার্থক}}
\textbf{\bn{সার্থক}} — \emph{sārthôk} — \textquotedblleft{}worthwhile; fruitful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তুমি} \bn{পাস} \bn{করলে} \bn{আমার} \bn{সব} \bn{পরিশ্রম} \bn{সার্থক} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tumi pās kôrle āmār sôb pôrishrôm sārthôk hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you pass, all my hard work will have been worth it.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সার্থক}} (\emph{sārthôk}) is Sanskrit \emph{sārthaka}, 'with meaning', significant (Monier-Williams). Bengali uses it for an effort that turned out to have a point.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sārthôk}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sārthôk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumi pās kôrle āmār sôb pôrishrôm sārthôk hôbe.} — If you pass, all my hard work will have been worth it.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to keep up, then the Bengali for to amend, then say \emph{sārthôk} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সার্থক} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Worthwhile; fruitful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বৃথা} (brithā)}{বৃথা (brithā)}]{\bn{বৃথা} (brithā) — in vain; wasted}

\label{lesson:BN-C383-britha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to amend, then the Bengali for worthwhile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বৃথা}}
\textbf{\bn{বৃথা}} — \emph{brithā} — \textquotedblleft{}in vain; wasted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সবাই} \bn{না} \bn{এলে} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{পরিকল্পনা} \bn{বৃথা} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôbāi nā ele āmāder pôrikôlpônā brithā hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If everyone doesn't come, our plan will be wasted.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বৃথা}} (\emph{brithā}) is Sanskrit \emph{vṛthā}, in vain (Monier-Williams): the opposite of \bn{সার্থক}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brithā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brithā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôbāi nā ele āmāder pôrikôlpônā brithā hôbe.} — If everyone doesn't come, our plan will be wasted.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to amend, then the Bengali for worthwhile, then say \emph{brithā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বৃথা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}In vain; wasted\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সন্তুষ্ট} (sôntushṭô)}{সন্তুষ্ট (sôntushṭô)}]{\bn{সন্তুষ্ট} (sôntushṭô) — satisfied; content}

\label{lesson:BN-C383-sontushto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for worthwhile, then the Bengali for in vain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সন্তুষ্ট}}
\textbf{\bn{সন্তুষ্ট}} — \emph{sôntushṭô} — \textquotedblleft{}satisfied; content\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{খদ্দের} \bn{সন্তুষ্ট} \bn{হলে} \bn{আবার} \bn{আসবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khôdder sôntushṭô hôle ābār āsbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If customers are satisfied, they'll come back.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সন্তুষ্ট}} (\emph{sôntushṭô}) is Sanskrit \emph{saṃtuṣṭa}, quite satisfied (Monier-Williams). What satisfies you takes -\bn{এ}: \bn{কাজে} \bn{সন্তুষ্ট}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôntushṭô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôntushṭô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khôdder sôntushṭô hôle ābār āsbe.} — If customers are satisfied, they'll come back.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for worthwhile, then the Bengali for in vain, then say \emph{sôntushṭô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সন্তুষ্ট} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Satisfied; content\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আক্ষেপ} (ākkhep)}{আক্ষেপ (ākkhep)}]{\bn{আক্ষেপ} (ākkhep) — a regret}

\label{lesson:BN-C383-akkhep}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for in vain, then the Bengali for satisfied.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আক্ষেপ}}
\textbf{\bn{আক্ষেপ}} — \emph{ākkhep} — \textquotedblleft{}a regret\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আগে} \bn{চেষ্টা} \bn{করলে} \bn{আজ} \bn{এই} \bn{আক্ষেপ} \bn{থাকত} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āge cheshṭā kôrle āj ei ākkhep thāktô nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I had tried earlier, I would not have this regret today.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আক্ষেপ}} (\emph{ākkhep}) is Sanskrit \emph{ākṣepa}, among whose senses Monier-Williams gives reproach and harsh speech. The Bengali sense, regret for what might have been, is not one the dictionary gives.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ākkhep}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ākkhep}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āge cheshṭā kôrle āj ei ākkhep thāktô nā.} — If I had tried earlier, I would not have this regret today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for in vain, then the Bengali for satisfied, then say \emph{ākkhep} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আক্ষেপ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A regret\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া} (bærthô hôoyā)}{ব্যর্থ হওয়া (bærthô hôoyā)}]{\bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া} (bærthô hôoyā) — to fail; to come to nothing}

\label{lesson:BN-C383-bertho-hooya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for satisfied, then the Bengali for a regret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া}} — \emph{bærthô hôoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fail; to come to nothing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পরিকল্পনা} \bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{আবার} \bn{চেষ্টা} \bn{করব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pôrikôlpônā bærthô hôle āmrā ābār cheshṭā kôrbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the plan fails, we'll try again.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{চেষ্টা} \bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হল}, \emph{sei cheshṭā bærthô hôlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া}} (\emph{bærthô hôoyā}) is Sanskrit \emph{vyartha}, 'without purpose', useless (Monier-Williams), with \bn{হওয়া}: to come to nothing. The taught \bn{ব্যর্থতা}, failure, is its noun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bærthô hôoyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bærthô hôoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrikôlpônā bærthô hôle āmrā ābār cheshṭā kôrbô.} — If the plan fails, we'll try again.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for satisfied, then the Bengali for a regret, then say \emph{bærthô hôoyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To fail; to come to nothing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Getting There to Worth the Effort}

\label{lesson:BN-R383-review-377-383}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for improvement and progress.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item improvement, progress, speed, to surpass, to accomplish
  \item preparations (for an event), without delay, a period of validity, to postpone, to chase up
  \item a pledge, a resolve, resolute, to break a promise, to vow
  \item favourable, adverse, suitable, qualified, to get used to
  \item an arrangement, effective, out of order, skill, to practise
  \item dedication, perseverance, to fulfil, to keep up, to amend
  \item worthwhile, in vain, satisfied, a regret, to come to nothing
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Improvement? (\textbf{\bn{উন্নতি}}, \emph{unnôti}.) Progress? (\textbf{\bn{অগ্রগতি}}, \emph{ôgrôgôti}.) Speed? (\textbf{\bn{গতি}}, \emph{gôti}.) To surpass? (\textbf{\bn{অতিক্রম} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ôtikrôm kôrā}.) To accomplish? (\textbf{\bn{সাধন} \bn{করা}}, \emph{sādhôn kôrā}.) Preparations (for an event)? (\textbf{\bn{আয়োজন}}, \emph{āyojôn}.) Without delay? (\textbf{\bn{অবিলম্বে}}, \emph{ôbilômbe}.) A period of validity? (\textbf{\bn{মেয়াদ}}, \emph{meyād}.) To postpone? (\textbf{\bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করা}}, \emph{sthôgitô kôrā}.) To chase up? (\textbf{\bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দেওয়া}}, \emph{tāgādā deoyā}.) A pledge? (\textbf{\bn{প্রতিশ্রুতি}}, \emph{prôtishruti}.) A resolve? (\textbf{\bn{সংকল্প}}, \emph{sôngkôlpô}.) Resolute? (\textbf{\bn{দৃঢ়}}, \emph{driṛhô}.) To break a promise? (\textbf{\bn{ভঙ্গ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{bhônggô kôrā}.) To vow? (\textbf{\bn{প্রতিজ্ঞা} \bn{করা}}, \emph{prôtigyā kôrā}.) Favourable? (\textbf{\bn{অনুকূল}}, \emph{ônukūl}.) Adverse? (\textbf{\bn{প্রতিকূল}}, \emph{prôtikūl}.) Suitable? (\textbf{\bn{উপযুক্ত}}, \emph{upôjuktô}.) Qualified? (\textbf{\bn{যোগ্য}}, \emph{jogyô}.) To get used to? (\textbf{\bn{অভ্যস্ত} \bn{হওয়া}}, \emph{ôbhyôstô hôoyā}.) An arrangement? (\textbf{\bn{ব্যবস্থা}}, \emph{bæbôsthā}.) Effective? (\textbf{\bn{কার্যকর}}, \emph{kārjôkôr}.) Out of order? (\textbf{\bn{বিকল}}, \emph{bikôl}.) Skill? (\textbf{\bn{দক্ষতা}}, \emph{dôkkhôtā}.) To practise? (\textbf{\bn{অনুশীলন} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ônushīlôn kôrā}.) Dedication? (\textbf{\bn{নিষ্ঠা}}, \emph{nishṭhā}.) Perseverance? (\textbf{\bn{অধ্যবসায়}}, \emph{ôdhyôbôsāy}.) To fulfil? (\textbf{\bn{পূরণ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{pūrôn kôrā}.) To keep up? (\textbf{\bn{বজায়} \bn{রাখা}}, \emph{bôjāy rākhā}.) To amend? (\textbf{\bn{সংশোধন} \bn{করা}}, \emph{sôngshodhôn kôrā}.) Worthwhile? (\textbf{\bn{সার্থক}}, \emph{sārthôk}.) In vain? (\textbf{\bn{বৃথা}}, \emph{brithā}.) Satisfied? (\textbf{\bn{সন্তুষ্ট}}, \emph{sôntushṭô}.) A regret? (\textbf{\bn{আক্ষেপ}}, \emph{ākkhep}.) To come to nothing? (\textbf{\bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া}}, \emph{bærthô hôoyā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Worth the Effort — once more}

\label{lesson:BN-R383-review-final-383}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for worthwhile and in vain.
\end{quote}

Worthwhile? (\textbf{\bn{সার্থক}}, \emph{sārthôk}.) In vain? (\textbf{\bn{বৃথা}}, \emph{brithā}.) Satisfied? (\textbf{\bn{সন্তুষ্ট}}, \emph{sôntushṭô}.) A regret? (\textbf{\bn{আক্ষেপ}}, \emph{ākkhep}.) To come to nothing? (\textbf{\bn{ব্যর্থ} \bn{হওয়া}}, \emph{bærthô hôoyā}.)
